name: Disrupt This!

pick.label: Pick a target
pick.heading: Pick something old-fashioned and disrupt it
lead: Every few years a start-up comes along and makes something we all do the old way cheaper, simpler or faster, and the big old companies say it will never catch on. Sometimes they're right. Often they're not.

Choose something from everyday life that is slow, annoying or expensive, and pitch the start-up that changes it. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The old giants are going to hate it.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I'm not looking for an amazing business plan here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some ideas will be the next unicorn, and some will only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: What did you pick from the shelf?
Queues, prices, forms, opening hours, that one person who is always rude…
A name and what it does. An app, a machine, a van, a robot, something completely mad?
What does it leave out that the old way insists on?
Who uses it first, and why them?
What the old giants will say:
And how you answer them, in one sentence.

values.annoying: You need an appointment to register your flat, the next free one is in eleven weeks in Spandau, and you have to bring a form that you can only get… at the Bürgeramt.
values.idea: Amtomat: a vending machine in every U-Bahn station. Put in your passport, smile at the camera, and your registration comes out like a Snickers bar. Seven minutes, no queue.
values.simpler: It only does the five most boring things (registering, a new ID card, a parking permit…) and sends everything else to a human being with a stamp.
values.first: Students and people who have just moved to Berlin, who have no idea where Spandau is and would like to keep it that way.
values.reply: They'll say a machine can't be trusted with something so important. They said the same about cash machines.

yours.label: Your start-up
yours.heading: Your idea

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which start-up wins?
rank.lead: Each student pitches their start-up in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
